key_insight: Physics-informed neural networks can recover dominant conductivity structures in the finite-data Calderón problem, and Fourier-feature encoding helps most when the conductivity has sharp localized features.
engineering_relevance: This provides a practical inverse-imaging approach for limited boundary measurements, with potential value in electrical impedance tomography and other nondestructive sensing tasks.
method: Train separate neural networks for conductivity and boundary-conditioned electric potentials.
Enforce the elliptic PDE with physics-informed residuals and fit finite Dirichlet-to-Neumann data with boundary losses.
Use randomized wavelet boundary excitations and compare raw coordinates versus Fourier-feature encoding.
evidence_signal: On synthetic finite-difference data spanning inclusions, sharp interfaces, smooth profiles, and heterogeneous media, the method achieved roughly 3%–12% relative reconstruction error.
watch_item: Fourier-feature encoding is not universally best, so coordinate representation and boundary excitation design need to be matched to the expected conductivity morphology.
paper_title: Recovering Sharp Conductivity Features in the Finite-Data Calderón Problem with Physics-Informed Neural Networks
